beats.intro: Learning module seven. [[sub]]How a swap is priced, and how its value changes over time.
beats.fra: [[pair]]A single period of an interest rate swap looks just like an F R A. The fixed rate payer pays a fixed rate, and receives the market reference rate, on a notional amount for one period. [[gain]]If the reference rate sets above the fixed rate, the fixed rate payer receives the net difference. [[diff]]One difference: an F R A settles once, at the start of its period, on a present value basis. A swap settles at the end of each period. [[same]]Otherwise they share a lot: a symmetric payoff, no cash upfront, and counterparty credit risk.
beats.series: [[head]]So why not just use a series of F R As? [[fras]]Recall the forward rates from our three government bonds: two point three nine six percent for year one, four point four five for year two, and five point one seven for year three. A series of F R As would lock in a different fixed rate for each year. [[swap]]A swap instead uses one constant rate for every period: here, three point nine six four one percent. [[vals]]Some periods have a positive present value, and others negative, but together the swap is worth zero at the start.
beats.par: [[eq]]The swap rate is the fixed rate that makes the present value of the fixed payments equal the present value of the expected floating payments. [[float]]Discount each forward rate with its discount factor and add them: point one one one oh one seven. [[fixed]]The fixed side is the swap rate times the sum of the discount factors, two point eight oh oh five four five. [[ans]]So the three-year swap rate is three point nine six four one percent. [[irr]]Think of it as an internal rate of return on the forward rates. [[net]]In year one, a fixed rate receiver gets three point nine six four one percent and pays two point three nine six: a net one point five six eight one percent.
beats.esterr: [[setup]]Esterr uses its swap to fix the cost of a floating-rate loan. It pays the lender M R R plus one point five percent, pays the dealer a fixed two point oh five, and receives M R R. [[s1]]If M R R sets at three point seven five percent, Esterr receives a net one point seven oh from the swap, and pays five point two five on the loan. Its cost: three point five five percent. [[s2]]If M R R is one point two five, it pays a net point eight oh on the swap, and two point seven five on the loan. Again, three point five five percent. [[q]]Every quarter costs about two point two two million Canadian dollars, whatever the rate does.
beats.bond: [[head]]A swap behaves like a pair of bonds. [[recv]]Receiving fixed is like owning a fixed-rate bond, financed by issuing a floating-rate note. It gains when rates fall. [[pay]]Paying fixed is like issuing a fixed-rate bond and holding a floating-rate note. It gains when rates rise. [[why]]That is why portfolio managers often receive fixed on a swap, instead of buying bonds, when they expect rates to fall.
beats.settle: [[eq]]Each period, the fixed rate payer's settlement value is the reference rate minus the swap rate, times the notional, times the period. [[curve]]Esterr's forward curve starts at half a percent and rises to three point seven eight percent over fourteen quarters. Its swap rate is two point oh five. [[p1]]In period one, M R R is point five oh. Esterr pays nine hundred sixty-eight thousand seven hundred fifty Canadian dollars. [[p2]]In period two, at point seven four, it pays eight hundred eighteen thousand seven hundred fifty. [[later]]Esterr expects to pay until period seven, and to receive from period eight on.
beats.time: [[head]]What is the swap worth after those first two payments, if forward rates do not change? [[pv]]Esterr has already made its net payments. What remains are mostly periods where the forward rate is above two point oh five. [[gain]]So the present value of the floating payments it will receive is now larger than the present value of the fixed payments. The swap has gained value for Esterr, simply with the passage of time, because the forward curve slopes upward.
beats.shift: [[head]]Now suppose instead that forward rates rise right after the trade. [[up]]Every expected floating payment grows, but Esterr's fixed rate stays at two point oh five. [[gain]]The present value of floating payments now exceeds the fixed: an M T M gain for the fixed rate payer. [[newrate]]A new swap today would need a higher fixed rate. Esterr locked in the lower one. [[loss]]If forward rates fall instead, the fixed rate payer loses.
beats.fyleton: [[head]]Fyleton receives a fixed two point three eight percent on two hundred million pounds, against six-month M R R. [[first]]The first M R R sets at point seven one percent. Fyleton receives two point three eight minus point seven one, times two hundred million, times one half: one point six seven million pounds. [[time]]With an upward-sloping curve, the passage of time works against the fixed receiver: after that settlement, the remaining floating payments are worth more than the fixed. An M T M loss. [[fall]]But if forward rates fall, the fixed receiver gains, just like the owner of a fixed-rate bond.
beats.wrap: [[w1]]A swap is a series of forward exchanges at one constant fixed rate. [[w2]]The swap rate equates the present values of fixed and expected floating payments; its value starts at zero. [[w3]]Each period settles the reference rate minus the swap rate, times notional and period. [[w4]]Rising rates help the fixed payer; falling rates help the fixed receiver, like a bondholder.
beats.finish: That's the end of learning module seven.
